goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14-19 — `record_for_host` matches on `uri.host` (no port), but the validation regex permits hosts with `:port` and the referer's port is discarded; a stored `example.com:8080` can never be matched and a referer `http://example.com:8080` will not match a stored `example.com`, so port handling is inconsistent between storage and lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost` the `host` field validation regex allows an optional `:port` (and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does not strip a port), so a record can be stored as e.g. `example.com:8080`. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(...)` and compares using `uri.host` (which omits the port) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored `example.com:8080` will never match a referer like `http://example.com:8080` (or any URL for that host). The finding’s statement that a referer with a port won’t match a stored `example.com` is incorrect (it would match), but the core inconsistency/bug about storing ports vs lookup discarding them is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:11-13 — `update` is a no-op that just re-renders the current state; the client's `saveChanges()` calls `embedding.update({})` against it, so the UI's save button silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` indeed does not persist any changes; it just re-renders `@embedding` (which is always rebuilt from `EmbeddableHost.all` in `fetch_embedding`). The client controller defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that no-op PUT route and effectively do nothing if invoked. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not include any save button or any call to `saveChanges`, so the claim that “the UI’s save button silently does nothing” is not directly verifiable from the diff. This is still a concrete, diff-grounded concern: an exposed update endpoint/client action pair that doesn’t actually update anything (likely leftover/incomplete functionality).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:4 — `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` side-loads only IDs and does not include the host objects in the payload, so the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` cannot resolve them; `embedding.embeddable_hosts` will not be usable records and the host table in embedding.hbs won't render properly

adjudication.rationale: In this codebase, `has_many ..., embed: :ids` is used to *sideloadd* the full associated objects alongside an `*_ids` field. The diff also updates the JS store hydration to handle plural `*_ids` keys (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` in `store.js.es6`) by mapping them into `obj[pluralize(subType)]` (e.g. `embeddable_host_ids` -> `embeddable_hosts`) and resolving them from the sideloaded root collection. So `embedding.embeddable_hosts` should be usable records and the table can render; the finding incorrectly assumes only IDs are sent with no sideloaded objects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-42 — for RSS/Atom feed polling (which doesn't go through `ensure_embeddable`), `record_for_host(feed_polling_url)` may return nil, so `eh.try(:category_id)` yields nil and imported topics lose their category entirely (previously defaulted to `SiteSetting.embed_category`)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import` the category passed to `PostCreator` was changed from `SiteSetting.embed_category` to `eh.try(:category_id)` where `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If no `EmbeddableHost` record exists for the imported URL/host, `eh` is nil and `category` becomes nil. The diff shows no fallback to uncategorized (unlike `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, which explicitly defaults blank category_id to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`), so this can create embedded topics without the intended category/default, regressing behavior compared to the previous explicit setting-based category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25-26 — `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises NoMethodError if the `embeddable_host` param is missing; parameters should be safely permitted/extracted rather than assumed present

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without guarding or using `params.require(:embeddable_host)`. If a client sends a malformed request missing the `embeddable_host` key (or it’s filtered out), this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500 the request instead of returning a controlled 4xx error. This risk is present in the diff-added controller at lines assigning `host.host` and `host.category_id`.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `before_validation` invokes `self.host.sub!` without checking presence, which will raise `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil. This is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:29 — host values from the site setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL without escaping; a value containing a single quote produces a SQL syntax error (or unintended SQL) during migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration loops through records from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting and runs raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` is not escaped/quoted safely, any host containing a single quote will break SQL syntax and could potentially alter the SQL executed during migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — the plural hydration branch maps IDs without filtering unresolved ones, so unknown IDs produce `undefined` entries in the hydrated array (the `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code since `map` always returns an array); the singular branch also leaves the original `xxx_id` key in place when hydration fails, an inconsistent outcome

adjudication.rationale: In `_hydrateEmbedded` (store.js.es6), the new plural branch for keys matching `/_id(s?)$/` does `obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and then unconditionally assigns `obj[plural] = hydrated || []` and `delete obj[k]`. Since `map` always returns an array, the `|| []` fallback is ineffective, and any IDs that can’t be resolved will become `undefined` entries. More importantly, because it deletes the original `*_ids` key regardless of whether hydration succeeded, unresolved IDs are lost (unlike the singular branch, which only deletes `*_id` when hydration succeeds). This is a behavior change introduced by the diff and can lead to broken/incomplete relations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1405-1407 — the test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" is now vacuous: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for hosts at all, so the assertion passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic; the removed host-count behavior is no longer actually covered

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `"is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets `embed_truncate` or `has_topic_embed?` to true, so it will pass trivially because the built (unsaved) topic likely has no `TopicEmbed` and `embed_truncate` defaults false. The added context that fabricates an `embeddable_host` also doesn't affect the method anymore, so host-presence behavior is not actually exercised by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:4 — no index is added on `embeddable_hosts.host`, which is queried (`lower(host) = ?`) on every embedded-page request in `ensure_embeddable` and on every feed import

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts` with a `host` column but adds no index. The model method `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and this is invoked via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` from `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, and during `TopicEmbed.import`, so the lookup can be on hot paths. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:29-32 — `cancel` does not reset `categoryId` after a cancelled edit of an existing host, leaving stale state that can be committed by a subsequent edit if the user doesn't touch the chooser

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6`, an existing host can only enter edit mode via the `edit` action (`editToggled` must become true), and `edit()` always resets `categoryId` from `host.category.id` before any subsequent save. Although `cancel()` for existing hosts does not explicitly clear `categoryId`, the stale value cannot be “committed by a subsequent edit” because re-editing overwrites it, and saving is only possible while editing.
